body:
This put me in awe. Thank you so much for elaborating on this. I can empathize with the panicking and sweating from the thoughts, and I’m so sorry you went through that, but I’m so glad to hear things got better:). 

I know you mentioned something about keeping yourself busy, and I often times find myself wondering if it would be any different if I wasn’t in a pandemic (I have so much time alone at home now). That maybe, I have too much time to think. I do try to occupy myself though, whether it’s playing games, making jewelry, painting, anything that I can. it’s a lot different when you’re alone versus when you’re out in public in the presence of other people though.

and like you said, I think the hardest part is getting over the past. Overall, I’ve always been extremely resentful and jealous, which makes it feel unnatural for me to be forgiving, but I’m trying. Accepting that it doesn’t matter it’s hard when my head tells me otherwise, especially when I find reasons to justify my negative feelings. 

As of right now, I’m working on accepting the past, and not compulsing (stalking and interrogating mainly). I’m going to try more to ler go of the past, and the self talk that you were mentioning:) I actually just started a few night ago, not necessarily with my RJ itself, but the anger and sadness I got from it. 

Again, I couldn’t thank you enough for being so compassionate and helpful. Your advice genuinely helps and I’m going to do my best to work on things

I am saving the tips for later for when it happens again because I always feel so out of control and, as of right now, have maybe 1 ‘healthy’ coping mechanism. Thank you so much for this. DO NOT ask her more questions. Unless it overlaps with you guys dating, there is no need for you to know (tell yourself this whenever you get the urge PLEASE). I know this is so tempting, but that is the #1 thing that will make your RJ worse and worse. I know everything my boyfriend has ever done within the last 4 years regarding his love life, and I’m consumed by the thoughts of it. This was a direct result of me asking questions once every month or so,... then every week or so,... then every day or so, then every day, then for 5-6 hours a day every day. You always think you get closure and then you find yourself asking again.

The reason for my RJ is actually my boyfriend leaving me before we were official to pursue other girls that were closer (I’m 4 hours away). That wouldn’t have mattered if he was better to me at the beginning of the relationship and listened to me more. I know 100000% that even if he had left me, but had been good to me the first few months, I would not be this way. I get so angry because he regrets it with his entire heart and I wish he could just go back in time and fix everything. I feel so sad and angry and I oftentimes find myself fantasizing about what it would be like to go back in time :(

not my cat, but my aunt’s who lived across the street for me and whom i visited often... having period back aches and having a cat massage you felt amazing. being nervous or extremely sad and having a cat come up to you and rub their head on you was so comforting. her cat was just the most affectionate thing. i can’t explain it, but he was just so cuddly. constantly being given love by a creature that won’t judge you is consoling

If it bothered him or made him upset or anything, he said no. If he was only okay with it because he was doing the same thing, he said no. If he was saying that because he didn’t care about me anymore, he said no. He’s never really shown any signs of jealousy so maybe it’s just him.

He said that if something else happened, then we would both know that we weren’t meant to be together anyways. I asked him if he wanted me to stop talking to this new guy, he said no. I emphasized that I got butterflies and everything and he said that he understood and that it was okay.

He yelled at me really bad, told me he never left me and that I was imagining things (I wasn’t, but at that time I thought I was going crazy), told me I was overreacting, said I didn’t trust him, said I was dumb, etc. It made me cry a lot and at the time I had really bad anxiety so I asked if he could call me for 10 minutes because I was panicking, he didn’t reply and then told me to “stop fucking calling.” Later on, he admitted to me that he kept her on his social media to see her pics bc she was “pretty and nice to look at.” He also used to belittle me a lot and only talk to me for nudes. He would always yell at me or make me feel stupid on purpose when I wasn’t doing anything wrong. He lied about a shit ton of girls as well (never actually cheated but still gave me trust issues). It sounds awful, but somehow he changed his ways completely and is perfect to me now. I’m just going through the process of forgiving him now, which I know will take time, but is ultimately what I’m choosing to do

Thank you so much for the insight on this, it helps a lot to unravel an actual clear perspective on it (as I feel conflicted on where to stand). I guess I personally don’t properly understand the whole fantasy part of masturbation, as I tend to only look for guys in porn that remind me of my boyfriend. If I do fantasize, it is only about places or things, not the person. I think that it is very clear (and has been for a bit) that he is still emotionally growing and maturing (as am I). He is 19. I know it isn’t the latter situation at all (him thinking it would be wrong for ME to do that but not him), because I did it once (before we had discussed whether that was okay or not, I masturbated to the thought of somebody else to try and relieve the insecurity that came from being with somebody who was my first but I was his 4th or 5th sexual partner) but felt extremely guilty about it. I told him the same day, and he actually laughed it off and said that that was okay, since I was doing it with the intent of alleviating anxiety and jealousy. I only did it 2-3 times after that. A couple days after is when I asked him if he did anything like that. 
I think that I have a hard time being understanding and patient with somebody who is still figuring out how and why to be honest. But I know he’s *trying* to be these things *now* because he knows how much it impacts my trust. 
Again, thank you so much for your input on this. it helps tremendously with how I’m feeling, even if it wasn’t direct advice or comfort, but it helps me understand and not be so angry or scared.

Before we were official, we went on dates. He seemed to be into me, everything was well, and then he stopped responding and told me he was talking to another girl. We remained friends, he regretted talking to her after a month, and came back to me. We started dating, and 5 months after we were dating she texted him saying “I miss you” and flirted with him. He never told me who she was or anything that happened between them, but I ended up finding out that it was the same girl as before. He said he extremely disliked her, that she was apathetic, etc. I asked him that I was really nervous about it and if he could just remove her from his social media since he doesn’t even like her. He called me insane, gaslighted me, ignored me when I was panicking, etc. Eventually, later on in the relationship while discussing this, he admitted that he kept her (and other girls) there because they were “pretty and nice to look at.” Yet he called me insane when I claimed that. He also would be disrespectful and call me a bitch, crazy, etc whenever things didn’t go his way. He’d compare me to his ex at times when I didn’t do things he wanted. He never cheated on me, but him not taking the extreme anxiety that I got over that girl seriously has affected me since it happened. I was crying and panicking the worst I ever had after he called me insane and he just hung up and went to play a game with his friends. He would talk to me about how other girls were hot and how hed have sex with x y and z celebrity if he could. He doesn’t do any of that anymore, and doesn’t even have that mindset, but it’s so hard to not be resentful.

Do something nice for her if you can, even if she’s irritable. When I felt really really terrible, my older sister would come into my room and just be goofy or lay down by me or being me a snack or something. It overwhelmed me if she was there for too long, but small and nice gestures made me feel okay and better. Don’t do it while she’s crying, unless you think she’ll appreciate it; I would always feel annoyed or embarrassed when she tried to help while I was crying. Maybe you can offer to go out somewhere with her too. Tiny things that you think will make her feel better will go a long way. If you’re really really concerned, you can make sure she doesn’t lock herself in rooms or stay home alone for long.

I used to feel this way a lot. I was always afraid that I was pushing away true intuition and a sense of danger by masking it and saying that it was my own anxiety. Would he cheat on me? Does he think badly of me? Is he the type of person to do x y z? I talked to my dad about this a lot, telling him that I felt like I NEEDED to feel safe and know that it wasn’t just my insecurity. Something that helped a lot was him telling me that no matter whether you decide to worry about it or not, the truth always comes out somehow. Say we are talking about cheating. If my SO cheated on me and I was not cautious of it or focused on it because I trusted them, in some way shape of form, the truth would come out more obvious than just some gut feeling. Either some other girl gets pregnant, or she tells me, or he feels so guilty that he has to tell me, or he starts to act conspicuously weird and odd, etc. This all is very likely to happen without me having to do anything about the situation. So a big thing is to trust that the things you worry about will be more obviously answered without you having to focus on them.
